extracted.intended_audience: inventors, employers, university administrators, patent practitioners and policymakers in Turkey
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of provisions in the Turkish Patent Code covering workers' inventions, higher-education and state-supported inventions, supplementary and confidential patents, contractual and compulsory licensing, and related obligations and procedures. Useful for determining rights, deadlines, and procedural duties under the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer obligations for foreign patent applications upon worker's request
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the worker’s request; the employer shall be obliged to give their rights on the invention for the foreign countries in which they do not wish to obtain a patent; and to provide the worker with conditions for making an application to claim a patent in such countries. Releasing the invention shall be made in a reasonable time period in terms of keeping within time period of priority right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer may reserve a non-monopolized right of tenancy (for a proper/decided fee) to continue using the invention in those foreign countries and may claim protection for interests generated from this reserved right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of employer provisions contrary to workers' invention rules; timing of contract authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations and applications by the employer against the workers in the manner of being contrary to the provisions regarding workers’ inventions shall not be allowed. The parties’ contract authorization regarding workers’ inventions begins, for in-service inventions, after the patent application; for independent inventions, after the worker’s obligation of notification to the employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements between employers and workers regarding in-service and independent inventions shall not be valid if not 'considerably equitable'; same for determined rates. Objections to inequitable agreements or rates can be made in writing at latest six months after the end of the business contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker and employer duties during patent application process
rubrics_metrics.description: The worker shall be obliged to provide necessary information and help to obtain a patent. The employer shall be obliged to provide the worker with copies of the application and supplemental documents and to inform the worker of progress during the application process upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before paying the rate demanded by the worker for an in-service invention, the employer must notify the worker if they renounce the application or rights; upon worker’s request the employer must transfer patent rights/documents at worker’s own cost. If worker fails to respond to notification within three months, employer can renounce the application and rights. Employer may reserve a non-monopolized right for a decent fee. Rights/obligations persist after contract expiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and objection procedure for independent inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a worker makes an independent invention while in a business relation, the worker shall be obliged to notify the employer without delay and provide information necessary to assess whether the invention is a true independent invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer may object in writing within three months of notification. Worker is not obliged to notify if invention clearly lies outside employer’s field. If invention is within employer’s field (or employer is preparing activities in that field), worker must offer employer conditions to benefit from the invention without releasing full rights; employer must respond within three months or lose preferential right. If employer confirms but disagrees on conditions, court determines conditions upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker's pre-emption right in employer bankruptcy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the employer bankrupts and the bankruptcy administration desires to transfer the invention separately from the business, the worker has a right of pre-emption on the invention he made and on which the employer claimed full rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances generated from the worker's invention are preferential balances; bankruptcy administration apportions such balances among claimants according to receivable rates. The worker may claim the invention as independent in return for his balance receivables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of workers' invention provisions to higher education institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions regarding workers’ inventions apply to inventions made as a consequence of scientific studies and research conducted in higher education institutions defined by the Law numbered 2547 and certain military/defense higher education institutions, without prejudice to special law/regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor must notify the higher education institution in writing without delay; if a patent application is filed, the institution must be notified. If the institution claims rights, it must file a patent application, otherwise the invention becomes an independent invention. The inventor may object; institution must specify written grounds or invention becomes independent. Articles 115, 116, 118 and para 4 of 119 do not apply to inventions made in HEIs. If institution renounces application or patent right it must first offer inventor takeover; if inventor accepts rights are transferred and documents delivered; HEI may reserve a non-monopolized tenancy for a decent fee. HEI must cover inventor losses caused by its fault. Revenue sharing: at least one third of revenue paid to inventor; institution’s share recorded as equity revenue and used for institutional research needs. Specific procedures determined by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for inventions generated in state-supported projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions generated in projects supported by State institutions must be notified to the supporting institution per regulation. Within one year of notification, the beneficiary must notify the supporting public institution in writing of their decision on claiming right ownership; if not, the supporting institution may take over rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beneficiary cannot make statements affecting patent/utility model until ownership process concludes. If beneficiary claims ownership they must file a patent application naming the supporting institution. The state institution may demand confidential commercial/financial updates and keep them private. Revenue-sharing form determined by agreement. State institution obtains a license at no charge for its own needs (renouncing this right only if specified in agreement). State institution may claim use or require third-party licensing in reasonable conditions if: (a) beneficiary does not use per Article 130; (b) product cannot cover public health or national security needs in other countries; (c) product cannot cover needs of the state institution. These license practices do not affect compulsory license provisions. Exceptions apply to certain R&D centers and technology development areas and to non-project-based state supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental patent application requirements and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may file a supplemental patent application to protect inventions that perfect or develop the main patent and are coherent with the main patent (per Article 91). Supplemental application may be filed until publication of the decision granting the main patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental application date is submission date. Search report prepared with main application's search report or later. Main patent is not considered state of the art for evaluating inventive step of supplemental application. A supplemental patent cannot be granted before the main patent decision. Time period of supplemental application runs from its filing date until the end of the main patent period. No annual fees for supplemental application/patent. Supplemental application may be converted to an independent patent application on applicant request during process. If Office detects lack of required connection, applicant must convert within three months of notification. If main patent annulled, surrendered, or invalidated for nonpayment, supplemental patent converts to main patent; decision on nullity does not automatically nullify supplemental patent unless not converted within three months after nullity notification. If converted to independent patent, annual fees apply from conversion date and protection period is as specified. Supplemental patents not allowed for utility models. Otherwise, patent provisions apply to supplemental patent where compatible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential (classified) patent procedure for national security
rubrics_metrics.description: If Office believes an application matters for national security it sends a copy to the Ministry of National Defense for opinion and notifies applicant. If Ministry decides confidentiality it must notify Office within three months; otherwise Office proceeds with normal processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If classified, Office registers application as a classified patent application and suspends other processing. Applicant cannot declare the invention to unauthorized parties. Ministry of National Defense may permit partial or full use of the invention. Applicant may claim compensation from the government for the classified period; if no agreement, court determines allowance considering invention significance and expected revenue. Annual fees are not payable while application remains classified. Office may declassify upon Ministry request; declassified application is processed from declassification date. If an invention made in Turkey concerns national security, no foreign patent application allowed without Ministry permission. Inventor domicile in Turkey is presumed until proven otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and effects of contractual patent licenses (exclusive vs non-exclusive)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application or patent may be subject to a license contract. A license may be exclusive or non-exclusive. Unless otherwise agreed the license is non-exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In non-exclusive licenses the licensor may use the invention and grant other licenses. In exclusive licenses the licensor cannot grant other licenses nor use the invention unless expressly reserving rights. Unless otherwise agreed, licensees cannot transfer license rights or grant sublicenses. Unless otherwise agreed, a contractual licensee may make disposals related to use of the invention during patent protection but must comply with conditions in the license; otherwise the patentee may enforce their rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to release technical information to assignees/licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise agreed, the assignor or licensor shall be obliged to release necessary technical information and documents related to the application or patent needed for regular use of the invention to the assignee and the licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignee or licensee must take due precautions to prevent classified information released to them from being revealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for unauthorized transfers and malicious behavior in assignments/licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: If it later emerges that the transferor of patent application/patent rights or the licensor was not authorized to make the transaction, that person is answerable to those concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is withdrawn, rejected, or patent nullity declared and parties failed to prescribe broader responsibility in contract, Article 139 applies. Transferor/licensor acting maliciously are always responsible. Failure to inform the other party of documents/reports in Turkish or a foreign language related to preservability of the application or invention or omission to include such documents in the contract may be accepted as malicious intent. Time to claim compensation under this article begins on the finalization date of the court decision that the obligations case is based on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public license offer publication and withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent applicant or patentee may announce in writing to the Office that they will issue licenses to anyone willing to use the invention; this offer is published in the Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any registered exclusive licenses exist the applicant/patentee cannot make such an offer. The applicant/patentee may withdraw the offer at any time; withdrawal is published in the Bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for granting a compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory license may be given if at least one of the following conditions is present: (a) the invention forming the subject of the patent is not used according to Article 130; (b) dependency of patent issues per Article 131; (c) public interest per Article 132; (ç) where TRIPS amendment protocol conditions are met regarding exportation of pharmaceutical products due to public health issues in other countries; (d) if a breeder fails to develop a new plant variety without infringing a previous patent; (e) if patentee carries out activities distorting, hindering or limiting competition while patent is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for compulsory license under (a),(b),(ç) are made to the court; under (e) to the Competition Authority. Except emergencies and (e), requests must include evidence that the requester failed to obtain a contractual license on reasonable commercial terms within a reasonable period. Court must send copies of request and evidence to patentee without delay; patentee has one month to submit comments with evidence. Court must decide within one month; if patentee does not object, court decides without delay. Judgment must specify scope, fee, duration, guarantee by licensee, start time, and measures to ensure serious/effective use. If patentee's evidence to stop the compulsory license is sufficient while remedies are pursued, use may be postponed until finalization. Compulsory licenses mainly target supply of the domestic market; special rules apply for plant breeders and mutual licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to use the patent (basis for compulsory license in disuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner or authorized person shall be obliged to use the invention protected by the patent. Assessment of use must consider market conditions and circumstances beyond the control or will of patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A third party may request a compulsory license if, after three years from publication of grant or four years from application (whichever later) the invention was not used, serious/real initiatives to use were not made, or use was insufficient to meet national market needs. This also applies when use is repeatedly interrupted for more than three years without justifiable reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licensing due to dependency of patent issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If use of a later patent is not possible without infringing rights of an earlier patent, a dependency exists: the owner of the subsequent-dated patent can request a compulsory license provided the subsequent invention produces a significant technical advance that provides largely economic benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a compulsory license is granted to the subsequent patent owner, the earlier patent owner may request a compulsory license to use the subsequent patent. If one dependent patent becomes void/null or expires, the compulsory licensing decision is eliminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license on grounds of public interest (public health, national security, economic/technological development)
rubrics_metrics.description: If use/increase/dissemination/improvement of the invention is of great importance for public health or national security, or non-use/insufficient use would cause serious damage to economic or technological development, the Council of Ministers upon proposal of the relevant ministry may decide to give a compulsory license for the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For inventions important to public health or national security, the relevant ministry secures approval from the Ministry of National Defense or Ministry of Health as appropriate. Compulsory licenses granted for public benefit may be exclusive. Licenses for national security may be limited to use by one or more businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal nature of compulsory license and fee determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory license is not exclusive in general, but compulsory licenses granted on grounds of public interest may be exclusive. Compulsory licenses are granted under certain conditions taking into account time, fee and usage area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court considers the economic value of the patent when determining the fee. For compulsory licenses granted per subparagraph (ç) of Article 129, the economic value in the importing country and non-commercial/humanitarian purposes should be considered when setting fees.
